red_flags.title: ITC beginning-of-construction cliff unverifiable — ~30% of project economics at stake
red_flags.evidence: Under OBBBA (July 2025) and IRS Notice 2025-42, solar >1.5 MW must document physical-work BOC by Jul 4, 2026 (no 5% safe harbor) or be placed in service by Dec 31, 2027, else ITC/PTC = $0. The dossier has no COD, no BOC evidence, and no tax-credit assumption, so the largest go/no-go financial variable is undocumented. Storage ITC under Section 48E survives regardless.
red_flags.benchmark: BOC by Jul 4, 2026 or PIS by Dec 31, 2027; KB values the credit at ~$60M on a comparable 180 MW-class project

red_flags.title: Interconnection position unknown in NV Energy BAA cluster process
red_flags.evidence: No queue position, cluster phase, POI, or network-upgrade cost estimate exists. The project sits in NV Energy BAA (NEVP OASIS) under FERC Order 2023 cluster rules where site control gates entry. Base rates: ~20% of queued projects reach COD, IR-to-COD ~5 yrs, network-upgrade cost shock drives ~30% post-screen attrition. Any POI relying on planned transmission (e.g., Greenlink West 525 kV, energizing 2027) carries multi-year delay distribution.
red_flags.benchmark: ~20% queue completion; ~5-yr IR-to-COD; executed cluster study with upgrade costs + 30-50% contingency required before COD claims are credible

red_flags.title: Desert tortoise protocol surveys and MSHCP coverage undocumented
red_flags.evidence: Clark County is Mojave desert tortoise (federally threatened) habitat. On non-federal land the Clark County MSHCP Section 10 permit applies (~$550/ac, ~$0.6M on 1,080 ac) and 100%-coverage protocol surveys gate layout freeze; the survey window is Sep-Oct and missing it costs +6 months. Any BLM nexus triggers ESA Section 7 plus elevated DOI review under EO 14315 / SO 3438 (confirmed live on BLM.gov). No biological survey, take coverage, or fee line item appears in the dossier.
red_flags.benchmark: 100%-coverage protocol surveys before layout freeze; Sep-Oct window; ~$550/ac MSHCP fee; Section 7 if federal nexus

red_flags.title: Land status and zoning jurisdiction unknown — BLM vs private vs Boulder City ER
red_flags.evidence: The 1,080-ac parcel's land status is undocumented. BLM surface or gen-tie crossing means 2024 Western Solar Plan conformance + FLPMA ROW + NEPA (Townsite Solar 2 precedent ~2-3 yrs, under IBLA appeal) plus elevated DOI review. Boulder City means the receptive Energy Resource zoning path (BCMC Title 11; 17,107 ac ER-zoned; city solar-lease program confirmed live). Unincorporated Clark County means a county SUP path. Timelines and denial risk differ materially; none can be confirmed.
red_flags.benchmark: BLM NEPA ~2-3 yrs local precedent; Boulder City ER zoning verified; jurisdiction determination is a threshold diligence item

red_flags.title: Storage configuration unspecified — 4-hr BESS is effectively mandatory in NV
red_flags.evidence: Technology is solar+storage but no storage MW/MWh, duration, or POI limit appears in the facts. NV procurement norms (Gemini 690 MW + 1,400 MWh at $38.44/MWh; PUCN Oct 2024 approval of 1,019 MW solar + 590 MW storage) make 4-hr storage the economic floor for summer evening peak; a token BESS fails market and offtake tests. The KB's analogous 180 MWac parcel carried 80 MW/320 MWh.
red_flags.benchmark: 4-hr BESS procurement norm; hybrid configuration required for credible NV offtake

red_flags.title: No offtake, revenue, or CAPEX documentation against NV benchmarks
red_flags.evidence: No PPA, LOI, or revenue model exists. Nevada has no CCAs; realistic offtake is NV Energy IRP solicitations, NRS 704B exits (MGM, Switch precedents), or data-center bilaterals. Benchmarks: NV solar+storage blended PPA ~$45-65/MWh rising ~9%/yr; >=80% of P50 contracted at close; CAPEX $1.43-1.56/Wac PV plus $200-350/kWh BESS (~$240-280M combined). None testable without the financial section.
red_flags.benchmark: >=80% P50 contracted; $45-65/MWh blended NV PPA; $1.43-1.56/Wac + $200-350/kWh BESS

red_flags.title: Long-lead equipment procurement status unknown — transformers are the schedule gate
red_flags.evidence: No equipment procurement, module supply agreement, or BESS integrator slot is documented. Market: GSU transformers 128-144 wks lead with prices +60-95% since 2019; HV switchgear 60-100+ wks; BESS slots 26-52 wks with FEOC-compliant cells (CATL/BYD excluded); Section 232 steel/copper tariffs at 50%; module MSAs need UFLPA traceability and tariff reopener clauses. Any COD claim without transformer POs already placed is not credible.
red_flags.benchmark: GSU lead 128-144 wks; switchgear 60-100+ wks; BESS slot 26-52 wks; >=6 months float between major-equipment delivery and COD

red_flags.title: Construction water, stormwater, and dust permits unaddressed
red_flags.evidence: No water budget or permit stack is documented. Clark County norms: construction dust control ~300-600 AF over ~2 yrs ($0.5-2M, trucked/hydrant sourcing), NDEP stormwater CGP for >=1 ac disturbance, Clark County DAQ dust rules Sections 90-94. Lake Mead record-low optics (Aug 2026) add reputational sensitivity to water sourcing though physical supply risk is low.
red_flags.benchmark: 300-600 AF construction water; NDEP CGP; Clark County DAQ Sections 90-94

red_flags.title: Community and tribal engagement plan absent amid politicized land-use climate
red_flags.evidence: No CBA, tribal consultation, or community plan is documented. The site is in Southern Paiute territory (Moapa, Las Vegas Paiute, Fort Mojave, Chemehuevi, CRIT) requiring consultation. Boulder City is structurally pro-solar (leases ~35% of city revenue, ~$17.2M/yr) but the July 2026 TS2 data-center fight politicized Eldorado-area land use; the project must be distanced from data-center narratives. CBA screening range $0.5-5M; <$1,000/MW is below-market.
red_flags.benchmark: CBA $0.5-5M one-time; tribal consultation before entitlement milestones

rfis: DATA ROOM INTEGRITY: Re-upload the complete diligence data room. The sole assigned file 'e2e-upload-probe.pdf' does not exist in the project docs directory; zero facts are extractable across all 11 components. Provide a full document index with the re-upload.

SITE CONTROL: Executed lease, option, or purchase agreements for all parcels comprising the 1,080 acres, with APNs, term (>= PPA tenor plus decommissioning), extension rights, and a current preliminary title report / title commitment.

JURISDICTION: Written determination of parcel jurisdiction for the site and gen-tie corridor — Boulder City limits vs unincorporated Clark County vs BLM-managed surface — with Clark County Assessor parcel map. This gates the zoning path, permitting authority, and NEPA/FLPMA exposure.
ZONING: Current zoning designation for each parcel, status of any Special Use Permit (SUP) application for utility-scale solar, and comprehensive-plan consistency analysis.
PERMITTING MATRIX: Complete federal/state/county permit list with current status, filing dates, and milestone dates for each permit.

UEPA: Legal analysis of whether a PUCN siting certificate under the Utility Environmental Protection Act (NRS 704.820-704.900) is required for the 180 MW facility and its gen-tie, and the status of any application.

INTERCONNECTION: Queue position in the NV Energy (NEVP) balancing authority area, executed interconnection request, FERC Order 2023 cluster study phase and results, network-upgrade cost estimates, proposed point of interconnection, and gen-tie route/length/voltage.

OFFTAKE: Executed PPA, LOI, or term sheet with counterparty identity, contracted MW vs 180 MW nameplate, tenor, price, and escalation; or documentation of NV Energy IRP solicitation bid status or NRS 704B exit application. Note: no CCAs exist in Nevada, so identify the actual offtake route.
FINANCIALS: Full CAPEX breakdown ($/Wdc and $/Wh for BESS), pro forma with P50/P90 energy, DSCR at P90, debt/tax-equity structure, and all tax-credit assumptions.

ITC STRATEGY: Beginning-of-construction plan under OBBBA and IRS Notice 2025-42 — 5% safe harbor vs physical work test — with target dates against the Jul 4, 2026 BOC deadline and Dec 31, 2027 placed-in-service deadline; provide supporting binding contracts/invoices if safe harbor is claimed. Approximately 30% of project economics (~$60M on a comparable 180 MW project) is at stake.

EQUIPMENT/PROCUREMENT: Module, tracker, inverter, BESS, GSU transformer, and HV switchgear supply agreements or binding quotes with stated lead times; FEOC-compliant battery cell sourcing plan; domestic content strategy; tariff exposure analysis (Section 232 steel/copper at 50%, AD/CVD on modules).
BESS SPECIFICATIONS: Storage capacity (MW/MWh), duration, chemistry, integrator, UL 9540A test data, and NFPA 855 compliance plan including fire marshal engagement.

ENVIRONMENTAL: Desert tortoise protocol survey reports (Sep-Oct window), Clark County MSHCP incidental-take coverage status, jurisdictional waters/wetlands delineation, Class I/III cultural resources surveys, and any biological assessment.
WATER: Water rights or will-serve documentation for construction dust control and operations, including any NDWR applications.
GEOTECHNICAL/CIVIL: Geotechnical report, grading and drainage plan, and FEMA flood hazard determination.
SCHEDULE: Integrated milestone schedule from NTP to COD including permit milestones, equipment delivery dates, energization, and the critical path to the ITC deadlines.
GRID INTEGRATION: Interconnection voltage, POI substation, reactive power and voltage ride-through capability, and ancillary services plan for the storage component.

DEMAND/MARKET: Market study supporting revenue assumptions (contracted vs merchant), NV Energy market basis-risk analysis, and alignment with the Nevada RPS (50% by 2030) and PUCN procurement of 1,019 MW solar + 590 MW storage.
COMMUNITY/TRIBAL: Public engagement plan, tribal consultation records, and disclosure of any organized opposition.
CORPORATE: Entity formation and good standing, developer track record with comparable projects, capitalization, and EPC/O&M contracting strategy.
ESCALATION: Treatment of a 10-15% escalation reserve and tariff/FEOC cost pass-through in the CAPEX model.
GEN-TIE: Route map, length, land status crossed (private/county/BLM), and right-of-way requirements.

agency_actions.agency: Clark County Department of Environment and Sustainability (MSHCP program)
agency_actions.action: Confirm Multiple Species Habitat Conservation Plan incidental-take coverage for the site and obtain desert tortoise protocol survey requirements and authorization to mobilize surveys.
agency_actions.why: Desert tortoise protocol surveys have a hard Sep-Oct seasonal window; missing it adds ~6 months and directly threatens the Jul 4, 2026 ITC beginning-of-construction deadline. Coverage status is currently undocumented.
agency_actions.deadline: 2025-08-15 (to mobilize for the Sep-Oct 2025 survey window; if missed, next window is +6 months)

agency_actions.agency: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Nevada Fish and Wildlife Office (Reno)
agency_actions.action: Coordinate desert tortoise protocol survey methodology, obtain occurrence data for the Eldorado Valley area, and establish the Section 7 vs Section 10 (MSHCP) consultation strategy.
agency_actions.why: Tortoise presence drives ESA exposure; the consultation path depends on whether a federal nexus exists (BLM surface or gen-tie crossing), which is currently unknown.

agency_actions.action: Hold a pre-application conference and file a Special Use Permit application for utility-scale solar (if parcels are in unincorporated Clark County).
agency_actions.why: Zoning status is unconfirmed; the SUP is the gating land-use approval and its timeline feeds the ITC BOC critical path.
agency_actions.deadline: Within 30 days of site-control and jurisdiction confirmation

agency_actions.action: Obtain written confirmation of UEPA (NRS 704.820-704.900) siting-certificate applicability for the 180 MW facility and gen-tie; if applicable, file the UEPA application.
agency_actions.why: UEPA applicability is unresolved; if required, the certificate is a statutory prerequisite to construction and the process takes roughly 6 months.

agency_actions.agency: Bureau of Land Management, Southern Nevada District Office (Las Vegas)
agency_actions.action: Conduct a land-status records check for the site and gen-tie corridor; if any BLM surface is crossed, file an SF-299 right-of-way application under FLPMA Title V and initiate NEPA review consistent with the 2024 Western Solar Plan ROD, accounting for elevated DOI review under EO 14315 / SO 3438.
agency_actions.why: Any BLM surface or gen-tie crossing triggers FLPMA/NEPA and elevated DOI review, which is schedule-critical and currently unknown.
agency_actions.deadline: Records check within 60 days of jurisdiction determination

agency_actions.agency: Nevada Division of Environmental Protection (NDEP), Bureau of Water Pollution Control
agency_actions.action: File Notice of Intent for coverage under the Construction Stormwater General Permit (NVR100000) and prepare the SWPPP.
agency_actions.why: Required before any ground disturbance on a site of this size; NOI must precede construction by at least 30 days.
agency_actions.deadline: At least 30 days before ground disturbance

agency_actions.agency: Clark County Department of Environment and Sustainability, Air Quality Management
agency_actions.action: Obtain a dust control permit for disturbance greater than 0.25 acre.
agency_actions.why: Mandatory for all construction in Clark County; 1,080 acres of grading requires an approved dust mitigation plan.

agency_actions.action: Confirm water rights availability or file appropriation/change applications for construction and operational water supply.
agency_actions.why: No water supply documentation exists; dust control for 1,080 acres requires a permitted source.

agency_actions.action: Initiate Section 106 consultation (if a federal nexus exists via BLM) or county-level cultural resources review based on Class I/III surveys.
agency_actions.why: Cultural clearance is a permit prerequisite; no cultural surveys have been documented.
agency_actions.deadline: Concurrent with NEPA kickoff or county permit application

agency_actions.agency: Clark County Department of Building and Fire Prevention / Clark County Fire Department
agency_actions.action: Submit BESS plans for review under NFPA 855 and the International Fire Code energy storage system provisions, including UL 9540A test data and emergency response plan.
agency_actions.why: BESS fire-code approval is a building permit prerequisite and a lender requirement; no fire safety documentation exists.

agency_actions.action: File Notice of Proposed Construction (Form 7460-1) and complete a glint-and-glare assessment given proximity to Boulder City Municipal Airport and Henderson Executive Airport.
agency_actions.why: Solar glare near airports requires FAA determination of no hazard; Eldorado Valley siting makes this likely applicable.

agency_actions.action: Obtain access/encroachment permits for site access from US-95/I-11 and any required intersection improvements.
agency_actions.why: Construction traffic and equipment delivery (including GSU transformers) require permitted highway access.

agency_actions.agency: Boulder City Community Development Department (if parcels fall within Boulder City limits)
agency_actions.action: Confirm land-use entitlement path and any city land lease requirements for Eldorado Valley parcels.
agency_actions.why: Boulder City owns substantial Eldorado Valley land; if the site is within city limits, the city — not the county — controls zoning and leasing.

verification_requests: NV Energy Transmission Planning (NEVP OASIS): Obtain written confirmation of the project's queue position, FERC Order 2023 cluster study phase and status, network-upgrade cost estimates, and the dates of the next cluster window. Base rates show ~20% queue completion and ~5-year IR-to-COD timelines; network-upgrade cost shock drives ~30% post-screen attrition, so the study results must be verified directly with the transmission provider.

Offtaker counterparty: Independently confirm with the named counterparty the authenticity and status of any PPA/LOI/term sheet — contracted MW, tenor, price, and conditions. If the route is the NV Energy IRP solicitation, confirm bid receipt and shortlist status with NV Energy procurement; if NRS 704B exit, confirm the application status with the PUCN.

GSU transformer OEMs (Hitachi Energy, Siemens Energy, GE Vernova, Hyundai Electric): Obtain written quotes confirming current lead times (benchmark 128-144 weeks) and pricing (up 60-95% since 2019), plus production slot reservation terms.
BESS integrator (Tesla, Fluence, Sungrow, or equivalent): Confirm delivery slot availability (benchmark 26-52 weeks), FEOC-compliant cell sourcing documentation, and price validity period.
Module supplier: Confirm executed supply agreement or allocation, AD/CVD exposure by country of origin, and domestic content qualification for the ITC adder.
Title company (First American or Chicago Title, Las Vegas): Obtain the title commitment directly, including all exceptions, mineral rights severances, and existing easements across the 1,080 acres.
Clark County Assessor/Recorder: Verify parcel ownership, APNs, and jurisdictional boundaries (Boulder City vs unincorporated Clark County vs BLM) against the developer's site map.
BLM Southern Nevada District Office: Independently verify land status records for the site and gen-tie corridor rather than relying on developer representations.
USFWS Nevada Fish and Wildlife Office: Request desert tortoise occurrence records for the project area and confirm MSHCP coverage applicability with Clark County DES.
Independent engineer: Commission a solar resource assessment (P50/P90), energy yield model, and BESS capacity/augmentation review to benchmark any developer production claims once provided.

Tax counsel: Obtain an independent opinion on the ITC beginning-of-construction strategy under IRS Notice 2025-42 (5% safe harbor vs physical work test) and FEOC material assistance cost ratio compliance.
EPC contractor: Verify pricing validity, schedule commitments, bonding capacity, and liquidated damages provisions directly with the proposed EPC.
Insurance broker: Confirm insurability and indicative premiums for the BESS (thermal runaway) and wildfire liability in Clark County.
conditions_precedent: DATA ROOM CURE: Complete data room re-uploaded and re-screened; all 11 components (state_law, federal_law, permitting, zoning, ecology_epa, community, financials, interconnection, grid_integration, demand, resource_supply_chain) must have extractable, quantified facts; readiness score re-run before any further IC consideration.
SITE CONTROL: Executed lease/option/purchase agreements covering the full 1,080 acres with term >= PPA tenor plus decommissioning, and a title commitment with no fatal exceptions.

JURISDICTION MEMO: Written determination of parcel jurisdiction (Boulder City vs unincorporated Clark County vs BLM) with the resulting permitting and zoning path confirmed as obtainable; SUP or equivalent entitlement secured or confirmed on a schedule consistent with the ITC deadlines.

ITC ELIGIBILITY (KILL CRITERION): Documented beginning-of-construction plan meeting IRS Notice 2025-42 with supporting tax counsel opinion — 5% safe harbor or physical work test satisfied by Jul 4, 2026, or a credible placed-in-service path by Dec 31, 2027 — plus documented FEOC material assistance compliance. No IC approval without this.

INTERCONNECTION: Executed interconnection request in the NV Energy (NEVP) cluster with Phase 1 (and Phase 2 if available) study results showing network-upgrade costs within a budgeted cap; any exceedance requires explicit IC waiver.
OFFTAKE: Executed PPA(s) covering >= 80% of P50 energy with a creditworthy counterparty and tenor >= 15 years, or an approved merchant/hedge plan for the uncontracted portion.
FINANCIAL BANKABILITY: CAPEX model including a 10-15% escalation reserve and explicit tariff/FEOC cost treatment; DSCR >= 1.20x at P90; sources and uses fully closed.

ENVIRONMENTAL CLEARANCE: Desert tortoise protocol surveys completed within a valid Sep-Oct window with MSHCP incidental-take coverage confirmed by Clark County DES; no ESA jeopardy finding; jurisdictional waters and cultural resources clearances obtained.
UEPA CERTIFICATE: PUCN siting certificate issued (if applicable under NRS 704.820-704.900) prior to construction NTP.
BESS FIRE SAFETY: NFPA 855 compliance plan accepted by Clark County Fire, supported by UL 9540A test data and an approved emergency response plan.

EQUIPMENT SECURITY: GSU transformer and BESS production slots secured under binding agreements with delivery dates aligned to COD and liquidated damages for delay; lead times verified against the 128-144 week (GSU) and 26-52 week (BESS) benchmarks.
EPC AND INSURANCE: Fixed-price, date-certain EPC contract with payment/performance bonding; construction and operational insurance bound, including BESS thermal runaway coverage.
COMMUNITY/TRIBAL: Tribal consultation complete and no unresolved organized opposition that would threaten permit timelines.
